en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
The Section on Offenses Entailing Confession (Pācittiyakaṇḍa)
At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the elder bhikkhus, while exhorting the bhikkhunīs, were receiving gains of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick.
Then it occurred to the group-of-six bhikkhus:
"At present, friends, the elder bhikkhus, while exhorting the bhikkhunīs, are receiving gains of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick."
"Friends, let us also exhort the bhikkhunīs.
Then the group-of-six bhikkhus approached the bhikkhunīs and said this: "Sisters, come to us as well; we too shall exhort you.
Thereupon those bhikkhunīs went to where the group-of-six bhikkhus were.
Having approached and paid homage to the group-of-six monks, they sat down to one side.
Then the group-of-six monks, having given the nuns only a very brief talk on the Dhamma, spent the day in trivial conversation and dismissed them, saying, “Go away, sisters.
Then those nuns approached the Blessed One; having approached, [they paid homage to] the Blessed One...
Having paid homage, they stood to one side. As they were standing there, the Blessed One said this to those bhikkhunīs:
“Bhikkhunīs, I hope the exhortation was successful?
“How could it have been successful, Bhante?”
“Venerable sirs, the group-of-six bhikkhunīs, after giving only a brief talk on the Dhamma, spent the day in frivolous talk and then dismissed us.
Then the Blessed One instructed, urged, inspired, and gladdened those bhikkhunīs with a talk on the Dhamma.

Then those bhikkhunīs, having been instructed, urged, inspired, and gladdened by the Blessed One with a talk on the Dhamma, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping him to their right, and departed.
Then, on this occasion and for this reason, the Blessed One had the community of monks assembled and questioned the group of six monks:
“Is it true, monks, that you, having given only a brief talk on the Dhamma to the nuns, spent the day in trivial talk and then dismissed them?
“It is true, Blessed One.”
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How can you, foolish men, after giving the bhikkhunīs only a brief talk on the Dhamma, spend the day in frivolous talk and then dismiss them?
This, foolish men, will not lead to the confidence of those without confidence…” [and so forth].
Having rebuked him … and having given a teaching on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks:
“Monks, I allow you to appoint a monk as an instructor of the nuns.”
And furthermore, monks, he should be appointed in this way:
first, a monk should be requested;
having requested him, a competent and capable monk should inform the Saṅgha:
‘Let the Saṅgha hear me, venerable sirs.
If it seems appropriate to the Saṅgha, let the Saṅgha appoint the monk named so-and-so as the instructor of the bhikkhunīs.
This is the motion.’
"Venerable sirs, let the Sangha hear me.
The Sangha appoints the bhikkhu named so-and-so as the instructor of the bhikkhunīs.
Whichever venerable one approves of the appointment of the bhikkhu named so-and-so as the instructor of the bhikkhunīs, let him be silent."
Whoever does not approve of this, let him speak.
A second time I speak this matter... [repeated] ...A third time I speak this matter—
"Let the Sangha, venerable sirs, hear me.
The Sangha appoints the monk named so-and-so as the instructor of the nuns.
Whosoever among the venerable ones approves of the appointment of the monk named so-and-so as the instructor of the nuns, let him be silent."
"Whoever does not approve, let him speak.
The Saṅgha has appointed the monk named so-and-so as the instructor of the bhikkhunīs.
It is approved by the Saṅgha; therefore, by silence, I hold this to be so."
Then the Blessed One, having rebuked the group of six monks in many ways for their difficult-to-support nature … [as before] … and furthermore,
monks, you should recite this training rule:
“Whosoever monk, not being authorized, should exhort the nuns, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).”
Thus was this training rule laid down by the Blessed One for the monks.
Now at that time, when the elder monks who were authorized were exhorting the nuns, they likewise became recipients of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick.
Then it occurred to the group-of-six monks:

“Friends, at present, when the elder bhikkhus who have been appointed exhort the bhikkhunīs, they receive gains of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick in exactly that same way.
Come, friends, let us also go outside the boundary, appoint one another as exhorters of bhikkhunīs, and exhort the bhikkhunīs.
Then the group-of-six bhikkhus went outside the boundary, appointed one another as exhorters of bhikkhunīs, approached the bhikkhunīs, and said this: “Sisters, we too have been appointed.”
“Come to us as well; we too shall give you exhortation.
Then those bhikkhunīs approached the group-of-six bhikkhus; having approached and paid homage to the group-of-six bhikkhus, they sat down to one side.
Then the group-of-six bhikkhus, after giving the bhikkhunīs only a very brief talk on the Dhamma, spent the day in trivial conversation and dismissed them.
“Go, sisters.
Then those bhikkhunīs approached the Blessed One;
having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, they stood to one side.
As those bhikkhunīs were standing to one side, the Blessed One said this to them:
“Bhikkhunīs, I hope the exhortation was successful?
“From where, Bhante, could the exhortation have been successful?”
“Venerable sirs, the group-of-six nuns, having given only a brief talk on the Dhamma, spent the day in frivolous chatter and then dismissed us.
Then the Blessed One instructed those bhikkhunīs with a talk on the Dhamma … [as before] … Then those bhikkhunīs,
having been instructed, exhorted, inspired, and gladdened by the Blessed One with a talk on the Dhamma, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping him to their right, and departed.
Then, on this occasion and for this reason, the Blessed One had the community of monks assembled and questioned the group of six monks:
“Is it true, monks, that you, having given only a brief talk on the Dhamma to the nuns, spent the day in trivial conversation and then dismissed them?
“It is true, Blessed One.”
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How can you, foolish men, after giving the bhikkhunīs only a brief talk on the Dhamma, spend the day in trivial conversation and then dismiss them?
This, foolish men, is neither for the inspiration of those without faith nor for the increase of those with faith…” [and so forth].
Having rebuked him … and having given a teaching on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks:
“Monks, I allow you to appoint a monk endowed with eight qualities as an instructor of the nuns.”

He is virtuous; he dwells restrained by the Pātimokkha, possessed of proper conduct and resort, seeing danger in even the slightest faults, and having undertaken them, he trains himself in the rules of training.

He is learned, a retainer of what he has heard, and a storehouse of what he has heard; those teachings which are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing, which proclaim the perfectly complete and pure holy life—such teachings as these he [possesses].
The teachings are well-learned by him, retained, mastered through speech, examined by the mind, and thoroughly penetrated by view.
Furthermore, both Pātimokkhas have been properly received by him in detail, well-analyzed, well-expounded, and well-determined, both as to the rules and their specific phrasing.
He is a person of beautiful speech and possesses a beautiful delivery.
He is generally dear and pleasing to the bhikkhunīs;
he is capable of exhorting the bhikkhunīs;
and he has never previously committed a grave offense against one who has gone forth under the Blessed One and wears the saffron robes.
“Or he is twenty years of age or more than twenty years of age—
I allow you, monks, to appoint a monk endowed with these eight qualities as an instructor of the nuns.
“But whoever,” it says:
Whoever is such a person … [as previously described] … a bhikkhu … this is the kind of bhikkhu intended in this context.
"Unappointed" means not appointed by a formal act consisting of a motion and three proclamations.
"Nuns" means...
"Ordained in both Saṅghas":
she instructs with the eight *garudhammas*; there is an offense of *pācittiya*.
If he instructs by means of another teaching, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If he instructs one who is fully ordained on only one side, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
That monk who has been appointed, having swept the courtyard, having set out drinking water and water for washing, and having prepared a seat, should sit down taking a companion with him.
The bhikkhunīs, having gone there, should pay homage to that bhikkhu and sit down to one side.
That bhikkhu should ask them:
"Sisters, are you in concord?"
If they say, "We are united, Venerable Lady," [the preceptor] should ask, "Do the eight weighty rules (garudhamma) prevail, sisters?
If they say, "They prevail, Venerable Lady," it should be handed over to them with the words, "This, sisters, is the exhortation.
If they say, "They do not prevail, Venerable Lady," they should be sent away.
“A bhikkhunī who has been ordained for a hundred years must perform acts of homage, rising up, salutation with joined palms, and proper respectful conduct toward a bhikkhu ordained on that very day.
This rule is to be honored, revered, esteemed, and worshiped, and it is not to be transgressed as long as life lasts.
A bhikkhunī must not spend the rains residence in a dwelling where no bhikkhus are present.”
This rule also, having been honored, revered, esteemed, and worshiped, is not to be transgressed for as long as life lasts.
Every half-month, a bhikkhunī must expect two things from the Saṅgha of bhikkhus:
the inquiry regarding the Uposatha day and the approaching for the exhortation.
This too is a rule: ...pe...
having completed the rains residence, a bhikkhunī should invite correction from both Saṅghas on three grounds:
by what has been seen, or by what has been heard, or by suspicion.
This rule, too...
[as before] ...a bhikkhunī who has committed a heavy offense (garudhamma) must undergo the penance of the half-month (pakkhamānatta) before both Saṅghas;
this rule, too... [as before].
A probationary nun (*sikkhamānā*) who has trained for two years in the six rules must seek full ordination (*upasampadā*) from both Saṅghas;
this is a rule...
[and so on] ...a nun must not, by any means whatsoever, revile or abuse a monk.
“This too is a rule...
[as before] ...from this day forward, the path of speech for bhikkhunīs toward bhikkhus is closed, while the path of speech for bhikkhus toward bhikkhunīs is not closed.
This rule also, having been honored, revered, esteemed, and venerated, is not to be transgressed for as long as life lasts.”
If he speaks on another teaching while the other is saying, "We are in harmony, venerable sir," there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If he speaks on the eight important rules (garudhamma) while the other is saying, "We are divided, venerable sir," there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If he speaks on another teaching without having delivered the exhortation (ovāda), there is an offense of wrong-doing.

If, regarding an illegitimate legal procedure, one perceives it as an illegitimate legal procedure, and instructs a factional community of bhikkhunīs while perceiving it as a factional community, there is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).

If, regarding an illegitimate legal procedure, one perceives it as an illegitimate legal procedure, and instructs a factional community of bhikkhunīs while being doubtful [of its factionality], there is an offense entailing expiation.

If, regarding an illegitimate legal procedure, one perceives it as an illegitimate legal procedure, and instructs a factional community of bhikkhunīs while perceiving it as a united community, there is an offense entailing expiation.

If, while uncertain that it is an illegitimate legal procedure, he instructs a factional community of bhikkhunīs perceiving it as a factional community, there is an offense entailing confession (pācittiya).
If, while uncertain that it is an illegitimate legal procedure, he instructs a factional community of bhikkhunīs being uncertain [of its status], there is an offense entailing confession.
If, while uncertain that it is an illegitimate legal procedure, he instructs a factional community of bhikkhunīs perceiving it as a united community, there is an offense entailing confession.

If, regarding an illegitimate legal procedure, one perceives it as a legitimate legal procedure and instructs a factional community of nuns while perceiving it as factional, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).

If, regarding an illegitimate legal procedure, one perceives it as a legitimate legal procedure and instructs a factional community of nuns while being doubtful [of its factionality], there is an offense of expiation.

If, regarding an illegitimate legal procedure, one perceives it as a legitimate legal procedure and instructs a factional community of nuns while perceiving it as a united community, there is an offense of expiation.

If, regarding an illegitimate legal act, one perceives it as an illegitimate legal act, and instructs a united community of bhikkhunīs while perceiving it as a divided community, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).

If, regarding an illegitimate legal act, one perceives it as an illegitimate legal act, and instructs a united community of bhikkhunīs while being in doubt [as to its unity], there is an offense of expiation.

If, regarding an illegitimate legal act, one perceives it as an illegitimate legal act, and instructs a united community of bhikkhunīs while perceiving it as a united community, there is an offense of expiation.
If, while being in doubt that the legal act is illegitimate, he instructs a united community of bhikkhunīs perceiving it as a divided one...
or if, while being in doubt, he instructs them...
or if, perceiving it as a united one, he instructs them, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If, regarding an illegitimate legal procedure, one perceives it as a legitimate legal procedure, and instructs a united community of bhikkhunīs while perceiving it as a divided one...
[or] if one instructs them while being in doubt...
[or] if one instructs them while perceiving it as a united one, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).

If, regarding a legal act that is legitimate (*dhammakamma*), one perceives it as illegitimate (*adhammakamma*) and instructs a factional community of bhikkhunīs while perceiving it as factional, there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
If, regarding a legal act that is legitimate, one perceives it as illegitimate and instructs a factional community of bhikkhunīs while being uncertain [of its status], ...pe...
or instructs them while perceiving it as united, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

If one who is doubtful regarding a legal act concerning the Dhamma instructs a factional Bhikkhunī Saṅgha while perceiving it as factional … or if one who is doubtful instructs it … or if one who is doubtful instructs it while perceiving it as united,
there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If, regarding a formal act that is valid, she perceives it as a valid formal act, and she instructs a factional community of bhikkhunīs while perceiving them as a faction, ...
or if she instructs them while being in doubt, ...
or if she instructs them while perceiving them as a united community, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If one perceives an illegal act as an illegal act and instructs a united community of bhikkhunīs while perceiving it as a divided one...
or if one instructs them while being in doubt...
or if one instructs them while perceiving it as a united one, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).

If one who is doubtful regarding a legal matter concerning the Dhamma exhorts a united community of bhikkhunīs while perceiving it as divided … or if one who is doubtful exhorts them … or if one who perceives it as united exhorts them,
there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).

If, regarding a formal act that is legitimate, one perceives it as legitimate, and instructs a united Bhikkhunī Saṅgha while perceiving it as a divided Saṅgha, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If, regarding a formal act that is legitimate, one perceives it as legitimate, and instructs a united Bhikkhunī Saṅgha while being uncertain [of its unity], there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If, regarding a formal act that is legitimate, one perceives it as legitimate, and instructs a united Bhikkhunī Saṅgha while perceiving it as united, there is no offense.
There is no offense when giving a recitation or giving an explanation.
When told, "Venerable one, restore [the person]," he restores them;
he asks a question;
when asked a question, he explains it.
If nuns hear one speaking for the sake of another,
or a female trainee (sikkhamānā),
or a female novice (sāmaṇerī).
[In the case] of one who is insane, or of one who is a first-time offender.
The training rule on exhortation is finished; it is the first.
